claim_boundary: numerical reference comparison only; NOT experimental validation and cannot substitute for Strantza held-out data

source.citation: Kaess M., Werz M., Weihe S., Residual Stress Formation Mechanisms in Laser Powder Bed Fusion - A Numerical Evaluation, Materials 16(6):2321, 2023
source.verification_status: setup parameters verified against EuropePMC fulltext 2026-07-16; complete Figure 8b and Figure 9a/9b PDF-vector digitization frozen as content-addressed CSV with explicit reading bounds 2026-07-27

reference_model.code: Abaqus, weakly-coupled (sequential) thermomechanical, implicit both passes, line search for convergence
reference_model.elements: DC3D8 thermal / C3D8 mechanical, 29568 elements total
reference_model.activation: layer-by-layer element activation via model change; supports initially solid (their build not simulated)
reference_model.release: partial separation from build plate at end via element deletion in lower support area (saw/EDM-cut analogue)
reference_model.heat_source: hemispherical volumetric Gaussian (Goldak-type), moving via DFLUX, absorption eta applied

powder_representation.type: explicit weak-solid elements switched powder->solid on melting via field variable

reference_model.mechanical_bc: bottom surface fixed in z and rotation; x/y partially permitted to avoid unphysical cooling tension
reference_model.thermal_bc: film 20 W/m2K + radiation emissivity 0.4 on top active layer; ambient = preheat temperature; bottom surface at prescribed build-plate temperature

geometry.shape: small cantilever over solid support structures (classic cantilever distortion specimen, few-mm scale)
geometry.reference_mesh_identity: 29,568 = 48 x 28 x 22 hexes: in-plane 25 um over 1.2 x 0.7 mm; z = 12 x 25 um (0.3 mm support) + 10 x 30 um (0.3 mm build). Uniquely consistent with all stated dimensions.
geometry.v06_mesh: 159_local/v06/benchmarks/kaess_2023/kaess_cantilever_c3d4.inp - beam+support footprint only (1.0 x 0.5 x 0.6 mm, powder margins unmeshed per v06 void semantics), 40 x 20 x 22 hexes -> Kuhn 6-tet split, 105,600 TET4, min quality 0.618, audit clean
geometry.status: partition inferred from element-count identity; support internal layout (full block vs comb) and cut/root extent still need Figure 3/7 digitization

material: 316L stainless steel (temperature-dependent tables cited in paper references)

reported_anchors.statement: all parameter sets produce upward cantilever deflection after support cut
higher build plate temperature lowers residual stresses; effect pronounced from 450 C
reduction of line energy density lowers residual stresses
tensile at surface, compressive interior, tensile at build-plate interface (classic three-zone profile)

use_limitations: This is a code-to-code comparison against a published FE study, marked as 对比实验; it provides no experimental accuracy evidence.
Reference powder E=10 GPa and absorption are author assumptions; quantitative mismatch does not falsify either model. Trend agreement is the acceptance criterion.

The frozen CSV contains the complete plotted Figure 8b 150 C vector profile and all Figure 9a/9b vector markers with conservative absolute symmetric reading bounds; these bounds are not standard uncertainty.
Geometry partition (cantilever vs support region) must be taken from Figure 3 before meshing; total-domain dimensions alone are insufficient.
